content: 1. Gospodarevskaya and Segal conducted a cost-utility analysis comparing different treatments for post-traumatic stress disorder in children who have experienced sexual abuse. This study was published in Child and Adolescent Psychiatry and Mental Health in 2012. 2. The London School of Economics and Political Science's Centre for Economic Performance released a report titled The Depression Report: A New Deal for Depression and Anxiety Disorders in 2006. This report is part of their special papers series (CEP Special Papers, CEPOP15). 3. Beck, Nadkarni, Calam, Naeem, and Husain proposed a strategic framework to increase access to cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) in lowand middle-income countries. Their findings were published in the Asian Journal of Psychiatry in 2016. 4. Rahman, Malik, Sikander, Roberts, and Creed conducted a cluster-randomized controlled trial in rural Pakistan, demonstrating the effectiveness of a CBT-based intervention delivered by community health workers for mothers with depression and their infants. This study was published in The Lancet in 2008. 5. Patel, Chowdhary, Rahman, and Verdeli explored ways to improve access to psychological treatments, drawing lessons from developing countries. Their work appeared in Behaviour Research and Therapy in 2011. 6. The World Health Organization (WHO) published clinical and policy guidelines in 2013 to address intimate partner violence and sexual violence against women. 7. Chisholm, Sekar, Kumar, Saeed, James, Mubbashar, and colleagues conducted a cost-outcome study demonstrating the integration of mental health care into primary care settings in India and Pakistan. Their findings were published in the British Journal of Psychiatry in 2000. 8. Salloum, Robst, Scheeringa, Cohen, Wang, Murphy, and colleagues conducted a pilot study on trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy (TF-CBT) for young children as part of a stepped-care approach. This study was published in Child Psychiatry and Human Development in 2014. 9. Patel discussed the future of psychiatry in lowand middle-income countries in an article published in Psychological Medicine in 2009. 10. Patel, Maj, Flisher, De Silva, Koschorke, and Prince conducted a survey for the World Psychiatric Association (WPA) on reducing the treatment gap for mental disorders. Their findings were published in World Psychiatry in 2010. 11. Murray, Dorsey, Skavenski, Kasoma, Imasiku, Bolton, and colleagues described the identification, modification, and implementation of evidence-based psychotherapy for children in a low-income country, specifically using TF-CBT in Zambia. This study was published in the International Journal of Mental Health Systems in 2013. 12. Tseng explored the influence of culture on psychotherapy, focusing on Asian perspectives, in an article published in the Journal of Mental Health in 2004. 13. Stoltenborgh, van IJzendoorn, Euser, and Bakermans-Kranenburg conducted a meta-analysis on the global prevalence of child sexual abuse. Their findings were published in Child Maltreatment in 2011. 14. Sumner, Mercy, Saul, Motsa-Nzuza, Kwesigabo, Buluma, and colleagues examined the prevalence of sexual violence against children and the utilization of social services across seven countries between 2007 and 2013. Their findings were published in the MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report in 2015. 15. Back and Lips investigated factors such as victim age, victim gender, and observer gender in attributing responsibility in cases of child sexual abuse. Their study was published in Child Abuse & Neglect in 1998. 16. Barker-Collo and Read reviewed models of response to childhood sexual abuse and their implications for treatment. Their work was published in Trauma, Violence, & Abuse in 2003.
